$comment: Coverage, so 'coverage has not dropped' can be checked rather than asserted.
CLAUDE.md §5 and the deploy gate both ask for it and neither could measure it:
there was no coverage tool at all, so the box was ticked on faith or skipped.
Not wired into `npm run check`, deliberately. Instrumenting every suite roughly
doubles the wall-clock time of a run that is already minutes long, and the gate
is something to run often. `npm run coverage` is what you run before a release
or when a number is in dispute.
The thresholds are the measured baseline rounded down by a point, not an
aspirational round number. A threshold that fails on the day it lands teaches
people to pass --check-coverage=false, which is worse than having none. The
point of slack absorbs the ordinary drift of a suite that talks to a real
Statements and lines are low because `all: true` counts every file including
the ones only a paired computer or a live provider key ever executes — the
worker's desktop layer and the office writers, mostly. Branches at 74% is the
honest signal here: the logic that is reachable without hardware is tested.
